speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. To help determine the cause of your dizziness and vertigo, can you describe exactly what the spinning sensation feels like and what triggers it, such as head movements? Also, how long does each episode last?

speaker: Patient
text: 70-year-old woman. The patient presents with sudden episodes of dizziness that are position dependent. She describes experiencing a false sensation of motion and occasional spinning, indicative of vertigo. She denies any recent illnesses, injuries, or significant changes in health status, apart from age-related hearing loss (presbycusis).

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that description; the position-dependence of your dizziness is a key clue. Given your age and history of hearing loss, could you tell me if you have noticed any recent changes in your hearing or balance, and whether you experience ringing in your ears? Also, have you noticed any associated symptoms like nausea, vomiting, or difficulty walking?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Episodes of dizziness and spinning sensation. I also have Position dependent vertigo, No recent illness, No hearing loss besides presbycusis.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV).

Given your age, position-dependent nature of the vertigo, and lack of other neurological or vestibular symptoms, I am confident in this diagnosis. Does turning your head in bed or looking up trigger these episodes?
